# media


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A profile media record names a local file as `asset:<sha256>.<ext>`, and
the host serves the file from its own origin. This module makes those
files. It does not download anything: fossick gets the source files.

[`clip`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/media.html#clip) and
[`still`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/media.html#still) run
ffmpeg. The module imports with no ffmpeg, and these two functions raise
`RuntimeError` when ffmpeg is not on the `PATH`.

## Assets

[`import_asset`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/media.html#import_asset)
copies a file into a store folder. The new name is the SHA-256 of the
content and the file type in lower case, so the same content always gets
the same name. The file type must be one of `MEDIA_EXTS`.

### import_asset

``` python
def import_asset(
    path, store
)->str:
```

*Copy the file at
[`path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#path) into the
folder `store`, named by the SHA-256 of its content; give its
`asset:<sha256>.<ext>` src.*

Two files with the same content give one asset:

``` python
d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
(d/'Tha.WAV').write_bytes(b'RIFF tha'); (d/'copy.wav').write_bytes(b'RIFF tha')
a = import_asset(d/'Tha.WAV', d/'store')
test_eq(import_asset(d/'copy.wav', d/'store'), a)
test_eq([p.name for p in (d/'store').iterdir()], [a[6:]])
a
```

## Clips and stills

[`clip`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/media.html#clip) cuts
`start` to `end` seconds of a file and stores the result with
[`import_asset`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/media.html#import_asset).
Audio becomes AAC in `m4a`, or PCM in `wav` with `ext='wav'`. Video
becomes H.264 in `mp4` with AAC sound, and the index goes at the start
(`faststart`), so a browser can play it before the whole file loads. The
size stays the same, made even for H.264, and never gets larger.
[`still`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/media.html#still) stores
one frame as a JPEG.

### clip

``` python
def clip(
    src_file, # an audio or video file that ffmpeg reads
    start:float, # the first second to keep
    end:float, # the second to stop at, more than `start`
    out_dir, # the asset store
    kind:str='audio', # `audio` or `video`
    ext:str=None, # for audio: `m4a` (the default) or `wav`
)->str:
```

*Cut `start` to `end` seconds of `src_file` into the asset store
`out_dir`; give its `asset:` src.*

With ffmpeg, a one-second clip of a generated tone has a duration of one
second. This cell needs ffmpeg, so it has the `slow` flag and
`nbdev-test` runs it only with `--flags slow`.

``` python
_ffmpeg('-f', 'lavfi', '-i', 'sine=frequency=440:duration=3', d/'tone.wav')
c = clip(d/'tone.wav', 1, 2, d/'store')
float(json.loads(run(['ffprobe', '-v', 'error', '-show_entries', 'format=duration', '-of', 'json', str(d/'store'/c[6:])]))['format']['duration'])
```

## Find a phrase in a transcript

[`find_span`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/media.html#find_span)
gives the seconds of a phrase in a transcript, for example to cut a clip
of one sentence. A transcript can be WebVTT text, a YouTube `json3`
dict, or a Whisper result dict with `segments`, each with optional
`words`, or with `words` at the top. A line or a segment with no word
times shares its time evenly among its words.

The match ignores case and punctuation. The words of the phrase must
come in order. Other words can come between them, at most as many as the
phrase has, so a filler such as “um” does not stop a match. The match
with the fewest other words wins, and then the first one. `pad` widens
the span on each side, and the start is never below 0. With no match,
the result is `None`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/rupaka/blob/main/rupaka/media.py#L102"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### find_span

``` python
def find_span(
    transcript, # WebVTT text, a YouTube json3 dict, or a Whisper result dict
    phrase:str, # the words to find
    pad:float=1.0, # seconds to add on each side
)->tuple | None:
```

*The `(start, end)` seconds of the best match of `phrase` in
`transcript`, widened by `pad`; None when there is no match.*

In WebVTT, the five words of the first cue share its two seconds. The
match ignores the case, the comma and the `<c>` tag:

``` python
vtt = '''WEBVTT

00:00:01.000 --> 00:00:03.000
The next stroke is <c>nam</c>.

00:00:03.000 --> 00:00:05.000
Listen: it rings, and then it fades!'''
test_eq(find_span(vtt, 'Stroke, is nam', pad=0), (1.8, 3.0))
find_span(vtt, 'stroke is nam')
```

Words can come between the words of the phrase, but the order counts.
“it fades” skips “then”, and “nam stroke” has no match:

``` python
test_eq(find_span(vtt, 'nam stroke'), None)
find_span(vtt, 'rings it fades', pad=0)
```

A Whisper result with word times gives the times of the words:

``` python
w = {'segments': [{'start': 1.0, 'end': 3.0, 'text': ' The stroke is nam.', 'words': [{'word': ' The', 'start': 1.0, 'end': 1.3},
       {'word': ' stroke', 'start': 1.8, 'end': 2.2}, {'word': ' is', 'start': 2.3, 'end': 2.4}, {'word': ' nam.', 'start': 2.5, 'end': 2.9}]}]}
find_span(w, 'is nam', pad=0.5)
```
